answer_summary: Brown calls FILLY a notably positive GA trial, explaining that APL-2 showed delayed but consistent slowing of geographic atrophy progression from 6 to 12 months and maintained some treatment effect after stopping. He also highlights real-world relevance because patients may have GA and neovascularization, including fellow-eye wet AMD, rather than cleanly separated disease states.

answer_limitations: GA-focused rather than nAMD treatment; article includes limited quotes and conference context, not a full Q&A transcript.

answer_summary: Brown attributes rapid aflibercept 8-mg adoption to it being a higher-dose version of a well-understood aflibercept platform. He says many patients can move from 2 mg to 8 mg without resistance and generally last longer, but expectations should be realistic because frequent-treatment patients may clear drug faster and need more injections than trial averages.
